A1.justification: Both PDFs describe TDDBench. Their main text, figures, tables, and complete appendices are readable and support comparison, including matching relocated and renumbered material.

before.justification: v1 reports original benchmarking experiments across image, tabular, and text data, including detection accuracy, computational costs, and sensitivity analyses.

after.justification: v2 retains the original benchmark results and adds experiments on vision transformers, Llama models, semi-supervised learning, defenses, and dataset size.

M1.justification: The benchmark framework and documented procedures for the original 21 detectors remain unchanged. New Algorithms 1–2 explain existing reference-model training and additional-query procedures; they do not establish a modification to the proposed methodology.

E1.justification: The same 13 datasets and three modalities remain, but v2 adds membership-detection scenarios involving semi-supervised targets and defended or label-only model outputs (Appendices A.3–A.4). These substantially expand the training and access conditions covered by the evaluation.

E2.justification: Figure 3(c) replaces MIN-K++ with PAC in the Pythia comparison, supported by the corresponding replacement of their descriptions in Appendix A.2. The other five LLM comparators and the main 21-detector comparison remain unchanged.

E3.justification: v2 adds ViT/Swin evaluations, Llama models from 7B to 65B, FixMatch training, four defense conditions, and target-dataset-size sweeps. It removes v1's query/reference-budget sweeps. The existing splits, metrics, default reference/query budgets, and original training hyperparameters remain unchanged; these are added or removed protocols rather than demonstrated reruns of the retained experiments.

E4.justification: New analyses test sensitivity to semi-supervised target training, dropout, label smoothing, output noise, label-only access, and dataset size. Conversely, v1 Appendix A.4 and Figure 4, which examine additional queries and reference models, are removed. This substantially changes the robustness questions investigated.

E5.justification: The stated five-repeat protocol, standard deviations for retained results, and 95% confidence intervals in the memorization analysis remain unchanged. No revised run count, seed policy, significance test, or uncertainty-estimation procedure is documented.

E6.justification: Tables 4–7 and the corresponding retained appendix results are unchanged. v2 adds Tables 8–12 and dataset-size results, replaces the MIN-K++ curve with PAC results, and removes the budget-sensitivity results. For example, newly reported Query-ref AUROC is 0.718 on ViT and 0.759 on Swin; these concern new target configurations.

T1.justification: The formal TDD problem definition and underlying assumptions are retained. Neither version presents theoretical propositions or proofs, and the added pseudocode explains existing procedures without introducing new mathematical results.

C1.justification: The central contribution remains a comprehensive multimodal TDD benchmark identifying weak overall detection performance, model-based methods' advantages and costs, and dependence on target-model knowledge. Rewritten contribution paragraphs and the shortened conclusion retain these claims; the additional experiments principally extend their supporting evidence.

C2.justification: v2 attributes weaker model-based detection under semi-supervised learning to mismatched reference training and discusses dependence on authentic model outputs under defenses. It recommends training-specific and defense-adaptive detectors and interprets the dataset-size experiment as showing no strong correlation. The earlier interpretation of returns from additional queries/reference models is removed.

D1.justification: The reported code-access location changes from an anonymous repository to a named GitHub repository. Appendix A.6.5 adds implementation-oriented pseudocode for reference models and extra queries. The original hyperparameter table is retained unchanged, and detailed configurations for the new experiments remain limited.

R1.justification: v2 adds citations supporting ViT, Swin, Llama, FixMatch, PAC, and its defense discussion, while removing MIN-K++ and several application-related references from v1. The positioning against earlier TDD benchmarks remains substantially unchanged.

P1.justification: The main section sequence and most existing prose are retained. Local changes include rewritten contribution paragraphs, explicit takeaway paragraphs, shortened related work and conclusion, reorganized appendices, updated author information, and acknowledgements. Most additional prose documents new experiments rather than extensively rewriting the existing narrative.

P2.justification: v2 adds five experimental tables and two algorithm boxes. The six-panel query/reference-budget Figure 4 is replaced by a three-panel dataset-size figure, and Figure 3(c)'s comparator legend and curve change. Existing appendix tables are relocated and renumbered while retaining their display structure.

improvement.justification: The new architecture and operating-condition evaluations broaden the evidence, but v2 removes useful budget-sensitivity analysis and introduces unexplained inconsistencies in its defense results. For example, Table 12 gives undefended CIFAR-10 Query-augment as 0.511, whereas retained Table 4 reports 0.573; several query-method entries appear permuted. Combined with limited documentation of the new settings, these issues prevent confidently weighing the coverage gains against lost robustness evidence and uncertain reliability of the added analyses.
